title: Attention leader on 1h: buy the nine-pair abnormal-volume leader on a rising 4h move, 6-hour cap

source.title: Hoang & Vo (2024), Google search and cross-section of cryptocurrency returns and trading activities, Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance 44

rule_summary: Chart 1h, closed bars, signal at close of bar t, fill at open of t+1. All nine pairs loaded as informative 1h pairs on the same timestamp. For each pair i: V4(t) = volume summed over bars t-3..t; Base(t) = mean of V4 at t-4, t-8, ..., t-168 (42 non-overlapping 4h sums, the prior 7 days; current window excluded); AV(t) = V4(t)/Base(t); R4(t) = close(t)/close(t-4) - 1. ENTRY for pair X when ALL hold: (1) AV_X is one of the two largest AV among the nine pairs (ties broken by larger R4); (2) AV_X >= 1.5 (volume activity filter, fixed in advance); (3) R4_X >= +0.6% and R4_X > median R4 of the nine pairs; (4) close(t) > open(t); (5) flat, fewer than 2 entries on X this UTC day, and no exit on X in the last 2 bars. EXIT, first of: take-profit +1.8% from entry; stop -1.0% from entry; time exit at the close of the 6th bar after entry (fill at next open). No higher-timeframe filter, no pyramiding.
mechanism: Attention-induced price pressure: Hoang & Vo find coins with abnormal attention earn higher subsequent returns, more so among large coins, with only partial later reversal. Abnormal volume concentrated in one or two of nine large pairs is the candle proxy for that attention; late retail buyers drawn by top-gainer and volume lists are the counterparty who pays, while the partial reversal is why the hold is capped at 6 hours. Cross-sectional ranking separates pair-specific attention from market-wide moves already tried (breadth thrust). Move per trade: target 1.8% vs stop 1.0% on bars already in high activity, so the average absolute move is near 1%, about 3x the 0.30% round trip; source has no intraday test, so this horizon is my adaptation.
